title: Oraciones, preguntas y peticiones
objective: Identifica el orden del sujeto, el verbo y sus complementos en afirmaciones, negaciones, preguntas y peticiones.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Uso del lenguaje

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct affirmative sentence.
options: The baker opens the shop at six.
Opens the baker at six the shop.
The baker open the shop at six.
The shop the baker opens at six it.
exercises.explanation: The baker es el sujeto singular. Opens es el verbo y the shop es el complemento directo.
exercises.hint: Busca el sujeto, el verbo y el objeto en ese orden.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “Nora ____ want milk in her tea.”
exercises.explanation: Con Nora, usa does not y el verbo base want para negar la afirmación en presente simple.
exercises.hint: Nora equivale a she. Revisa qué auxiliar sigue a she.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct question about an event last Saturday.
options: Where did Eli left his jacket?
Where Eli did leave his jacket?
Where did Eli leave his jacket?
Where does Eli left his jacket?
exercises.explanation: Did expresa el pasado. El sujeto Eli va después del auxiliar y leave conserva la forma base.
exercises.hint: Busca una estructura con where, did, sujeto y verbo base.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a polite request?
options: Could you move your bag, please?
You could moved your bag, please.
Could move you your bag, please?
Could you to move your bag, please?
exercises.explanation: Could va antes del sujeto you y se combina con el verbo base move. Please refuerza la cortesía.
exercises.hint: Identifica el verbo base de la acción que se pide.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence in which the adjective comes after the verb and describes the subject.
exercises.explanation: Fresh va después de smells y describe al sujeto de la oración, the soup.
exercises.hint: Ubica un adjetivo después de un verbo que describa un estado o una impresión.

exercises.prompt: Complete the embedded question. “Can you tell me ____?”
options: where does the meeting room is
exercises.explanation: En la pregunta indirecta, el sujeto the meeting room precede a is. Can you tell me ya establece la estructura interrogativa principal.
exercises.hint: Dentro de la pregunta, conserva el orden de una afirmación.

exercises.prompt: In which sentence does Maya receive a schedule from the coach?
options: Maya gave the coach a schedule.
The coach gave a schedule to himself.
The coach gave Maya a schedule.
The schedule gave Maya a coach.
exercises.explanation: The coach realiza la acción. Maya es quien recibe el horario y a schedule nombra el objeto entregado.
exercises.hint: Busca quién entrega algo, quién lo recibe y qué se entrega.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word order for a question about where Mia lives.
exercises.explanation: El orden es where, does, Mia y live. El verbo principal usa la forma base después de does.
exercises.hint: En una pregunta con where, coloca el auxiliar antes del sujeto.

exercises.prompt: Complete the polite request. “Would you mind ____ the window?”
exercises.explanation: Después de Would you mind se usa la forma en -ing. La petición completa es «Would you mind closing the window?»
exercises.hint: Busca la forma verbal que sigue a mind en esta petición.

title: Tiempos verbales y voz pasiva
objective: Reconoce el tiempo, la concordancia y las formas activas y pasivas de los verbos.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Uso del lenguaje

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “Every morning, Leo ____ the windows before class.”
exercises.explanation: Every morning señala una rutina. Leo equivale a he, por lo que opens lleva -s en presente simple.
exercises.hint: Comprueba el tiempo de la rutina y el número del sujeto.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “Look! The children ____ a kite.”
exercises.explanation: Look indica una acción que se puede ver ahora. El sujeto plural the children se combina con are flying.
exercises.hint: Identifica la forma de be para un sujeto plural y una acción en curso.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “When the lights went out, I ____ dinner.”
exercises.explanation: Went out señala un hecho pasado. Was cooking describe la acción que estaba en curso en ese momento.
exercises.hint: Busca la acción en curso y el hecho breve en pasado.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: Two students were painting the mural.
The mural looked bright after the art class.
The mural was painted by two students.
exercises.explanation: El mural recibe la acción. Was painted combina be en pasado con el participio painted.
exercises.hint: Busca be seguido del participio de un verbo de acción.

exercises.prompt: Complete the prediction. “I think the buses ____ on time tomorrow.”
exercises.explanation: Tomorrow sitúa la predicción en el futuro. Después de will, el verbo toma la forma base arrive.
exercises.hint: Si eliges will, revisa la forma del verbo que lo sigue.

exercises.prompt: Complete the notice. “These forms must ____ before the office closes.”
exercises.explanation: Los formularios reciben la acción. Después de must, usa be y el participio signed para formar la voz pasiva.
exercises.hint: Identifica qué recibe la acción y coloca be antes del participio.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence about an experiment that did not happen. “If we ____ the seeds earlier, we would have seen the results by now.”
exercises.explanation: Had planted expresa la condición imaginaria sobre una acción pasada. Would have seen expresa el resultado imaginado.
exercises.hint: Busca el auxiliar had y el participio para la condición anterior.

exercises.prompt: Complete the negative sentence. “Yesterday, Jules ____ take the bus.”
exercises.explanation: Did not forma la negación del pasado simple. El verbo take conserva su forma base.
exercises.hint: Yesterday indica que la acción se sitúa en el pasado.

exercises.prompt: Complete the report about a repair finished yesterday. “The broken lamps ____ by the electrician.”
exercises.explanation: Lamps recibe la acción. Se usa were con el sujeto plural y replaced como participio.
exercises.hint: Usa voz pasiva en pasado. El sujeto lamps es plural.

title: Sustantivos, adjetivos y adverbios
objective: Distingue plurales comunes e irregulares, posesivos, orden de adjetivos, comparaciones y posición de adverbios.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Uso del lenguaje

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “Three ____ ran across the playground.”
exercises.explanation: Three exige un plural. El plural irregular de child es children.
exercises.hint: Distingue una forma plural de una forma posesiva.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “the projects made by two students”?
exercises.explanation: El plural students termina en s. Para marcar la posesión en ese caso, coloca solo un apóstrofo después de la s.
exercises.hint: Primero forma el plural students. Luego añade el signo de posesión.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “This route is ____ than the old route.” (short)
exercises.explanation: Than introduce la segunda ruta de la comparación. Para el adjetivo corto short, usa shorter.
exercises.hint: Busca la forma en -er que se combina con than.

exercises.prompt: Choose the phrase with the usual adjective order.
exercises.explanation: El orden habitual coloca el tamaño small, después el color green y al final el material metal antes del sustantivo.
exercises.hint: Ordena los datos por tamaño, color y material.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “Of all the times today, Aria’s was ____.” (good)
exercises.explanation: Of all the times indica un grupo completo. El superlativo irregular de good es best.
exercises.hint: Distingue entre comparar dos tiempos y escoger el principal de todo el grupo.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “The puzzle was ____ and the students felt ____.”
exercises.explanation: Confusing describe el efecto que produce el rompecabezas. Confused describe cómo se sentían los estudiantes.
exercises.hint: Distingue la fuente de la sensación de las personas que la experimentan.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that says when Ken spoke and how he spoke.
options: Ken often spoke near the door.
Ken spoke after lunch in the courtyard.
exercises.explanation: Softly explica cómo habló Ken. After lunch indica cuándo ocurrió.
exercises.hint: Busca una expresión de tiempo y otra de modo en la misma oración.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “Two ____ were asleep in the barn.”
exercises.explanation: El plural de mouse es mice. Two indica que se necesita un sustantivo plural.
exercises.hint: Mouse tiene un plural irregular.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says that only three students came to class because there was a storm?
options: Because of the storm, only three students came to class.
Nearly three students missed class during the storm.
Three students nearly missed class during the storm.
The storm started when three students left class.
exercises.explanation: Only modifica a three students y limita a tres el número de asistentes. Because of the storm da la causa.
exercises.hint: Busca only junto a la cantidad que se quiere limitar.

title: Preposiciones, pronombres y determinantes
objective: Elige palabras que expresan lugar, tiempo, posesión, cantidad o relación entre ideas.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Uso del lenguaje

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “The workshop starts ____ 9:30 on Tuesday.”
exercises.explanation: At introduce una hora concreta. On Tuesday, que ya aparece al final, señala el día.
exercises.hint: Distingue la hora del día de la semana.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “____ books on this desk belong to Maya.”
exercises.explanation: Books es plural. These indica que los libros están cerca, como sugiere on this desk.
exercises.hint: Identifica el número del sustantivo books.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “The librarian gave the atlas to Luis and ____.”
exercises.explanation: La preposición to introduce a quienes reciben el atlas. Me es la forma de objeto.
exercises.hint: Prueba la misma construcción con «to ____» y omite Luis and.

exercises.prompt: Complete the question. “How ____ information did you find about the festival?”
exercises.explanation: Information es un sustantivo no contable en inglés. En la pregunta, se usa how much para consultar su cantidad.
exercises.hint: Determina si information se usa como un sustantivo contable.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “There is one bench on each side of the lamp. The lamp stands ____ the two benches.”
exercises.explanation: Between expresa que la lámpara queda en el espacio entre los dos bancos.
exercises.hint: Dibuja los dos bancos y coloca la lámpara según lo indica la primera frase.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “That scarf belongs to Carla. It is ____.”
exercises.explanation: Hers reemplaza la frase her scarf. Her debe acompañar a un sustantivo si funciona como determinante posesivo.
exercises.hint: Busca la forma que puede funcionar sola y expresa pertenencia.

exercises.prompt: Choose the word that makes the second idea the reason for the first. “We moved the class indoors ____ the wind had become too strong.”
exercises.explanation: Because presenta el viento fuerte como la causa de trasladar la clase.
exercises.hint: Haz que la segunda parte responda a «why?».

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “The science fair takes place ____ Friday.”
exercises.explanation: En inglés se usa on con días de la semana. La expresión correcta es on Friday.
exercises.hint: Identifica si Friday es un día, un mes o una hora.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence. “We have enough flour, but we need ____ eggs to make the cake.”
exercises.explanation: A few more expresa una pequeña cantidad adicional con un sustantivo plural contable. A little more se usa con sustancias como flour.
exercises.hint: Eggs es un sustantivo plural que se puede contar.

title: Detalles, secuencia e inferencias
objective: Localiza evidencia en inglés para reconocer detalles, ordenar hechos e inferir conclusiones.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Comprensión y análisis de lectura

exercises.prompt:
The school library added a return slot that families could reach from the sidewalk. It was beside the side entrance, which staff locked every evening. After one month, the library counted 64 books returned through the slot. Staff decided to keep it open on weekends.

Where was the return slot installed?
exercises.explanation: La segunda oración dice «It was beside the side entrance». La ranura estaba junto a la entrada lateral.
exercises.hint: Busca la primera aparición de return slot.

exercises.prompt:
Read the passage. “After packing the lunches, Al took the keys from the shelf. Before he packed the lunches, he fed the cat. He left at seven.”

What happened first?
exercises.explanation: Before he packed the lunches coloca la comida del gato antes de preparar los almuerzos. Las llaves y la salida ocurrieron después.
exercises.hint: Ubica qué hizo Al antes de preparar los almuerzos.

exercises.prompt:
Read the passage. “The path was narrow. Two people could not walk side by side.”

What does narrow mean here?
exercises.explanation: La segunda oración describe el ancho insuficiente para dos personas. Narrow significa estrecho.
exercises.hint: Relaciona «side by side» con una dimensión del camino.

exercises.prompt:
The town tested two bicycle routes to the beach. The river route was shorter, but the path often flooded in the afternoon. The hill route was longer and stayed dry throughout the test. The town printed the hill route on its summer maps and plans to check both routes again in winter.

What made the river route difficult to use during the test?
exercises.explanation: El camino junto al río se inundaba con frecuencia por la tarde. Eso dificultaba usarlo.
exercises.hint: Busca el problema asociado con river route.

exercises.prompt:
The town tested two bicycle routes to the beach. The river route was shorter, but the path often flooded in the afternoon. The hill route was longer and stayed dry throughout the test. The town printed the hill route on its summer maps and plans to check both routes again in winter.

Which is the best title?
options: Choosing a Summer Bike Route to the Beach
The Shortest Bike Routes in the World
When to Buy a New Bicycle
A Winter Guide to the Town’s Rivers
exercises.explanation: El título reúne el tema, dos rutas a la playa, y el enfoque, escoger una para los mapas de verano.
exercises.hint: Identifica tanto el destino como la decisión principal del pueblo.

exercises.prompt:
The school library added a return slot that families could reach from the sidewalk. It was beside the side entrance, which staff locked every evening. After one month, the library counted 64 books returned through the slot. Staff decided to keep it open on weekends.

What can reasonably be inferred?
options: The library then shortened its opening hours.
Families could return books without going into the library.
All families used the slot every weekend.
The new slot accepts only weekend returns.
exercises.explanation: La ranura queda al alcance desde la acera. Las personas devolvieron 64 libros por ella. Por lo tanto, la devolución no requiere entrar a la biblioteca.
exercises.hint: Relaciona el acceso desde la acera con el número de libros devueltos.

exercises.prompt:
The town tested two bicycle routes to the beach. The river route was shorter, but the path often flooded in the afternoon. The hill route was longer and stayed dry throughout the test. The town printed the hill route on its summer maps and plans to check both routes again in winter.

Which conclusion is supported by the passage?
options: The town showed that longer routes are always safer.
The river route will never appear on a map.
The town chose the route that stayed dry during the test.
exercises.explanation: El texto solo respalda la decisión de verano y lo observado durante el ensayo. Los planes de invierno siguen abiertos.
exercises.hint: Elige la conclusión limitada a lo que el pueblo observó y decidió.

exercises.prompt:
The town tested two bicycle routes to the beach. The river route was shorter, but the path often flooded in the afternoon. The hill route was longer and stayed dry throughout the test. The town printed the hill route on its summer maps and plans to check both routes again in winter.

Which statement is an opinion?
options: The hill route stayed dry during the test.
The hill route is the most enjoyable way to reach the beach.
The town plans another check in winter.
exercises.explanation: Most enjoyable expresa un juicio sobre lo que se disfruta. Las otras opciones se pueden comprobar con el relato.
exercises.hint: Busca una valoración personal.

exercises.prompt:
Mina wanted to return a borrowed jacket. She folded it at home, carried it to school in a tote bag, and handed it to Eli before lunch.

Where did Mina fold the jacket?
exercises.explanation: El texto dice «She folded it at home». Mina dobló la chaqueta en casa.
exercises.hint: Busca la expresión de lugar que aparece justo después de folded it.

exercises.prompt:
The community center lent out umbrellas on rainy days. At first, visitors left them in a bin after turning them in. Several wet umbrellas stayed in the bin overnight. The center then added a drying rack next to the returns counter.

Why did the center most likely add the drying rack?
options: To collect money for more umbrellas
To give returned umbrellas a place to dry
To give visitors a place to buy umbrellas
To stop visitors from returning umbrellas
exercises.explanation: Las sombrillas seguían mojadas en el contenedor. El nuevo soporte permite dejar abiertas las sombrillas devueltas para que se sequen.
exercises.hint: Relaciona el problema de las sombrillas mojadas con el uso de un drying rack.

title: Personajes, propósito y lenguaje figurado
objective: Reconoce personajes, ambiente, punto de vista, conflictos, tono y tipo de texto.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Comprensión y análisis de lectura

exercises.prompt:
“I read my name on the list and imagined the whole room laughing. During practice, I missed the first line twice. On Thursday, my brother sat in the front row with his notebook. I felt my face grow hot as I walked onstage. Then I spotted his smile and took a breath. The words came out, one by one.”

Who tells the story?
options: The brother in the front row.
exercises.explanation: El narrador usa I y cuenta que subió al escenario. El hermano aparece como otro personaje.
exercises.hint: Identifica a quién se refiere «I» en «I walked onstage».

exercises.prompt:
The wooden bridge was closed when Mari arrived at the trail. She could see the picnic area on the other side, but there was no safe way across the creek. She followed the signs to a stone crossing a little farther upstream.

Where do the events take place?
options: On a trail near a creek.
In a house near the ocean.
exercises.explanation: Trail, creek y upstream sitúan la acción en un sendero cerca de un arroyo.
exercises.hint: Busca palabras que nombren lugares.

exercises.prompt:
The wooden bridge was closed when Mari arrived at the trail. She could see the picnic area on the other side, but there was no safe way across the creek. She followed the signs to a stone crossing a little farther upstream.

Which type of conflict does Mari face?
options: A character against her own doubts.
A character against an unfair school rule.
A character against an obstacle in the environment.
exercises.explanation: El puente cerrado y el arroyo dificultan el recorrido. Son obstáculos exteriores que Mari resuelve al buscar otro cruce.
exercises.hint: Identifica qué impide que Mari llegue directamente al área de picnic.

exercises.prompt:
Read the sentence. “The old gate groaned like a tired runner.”

What kind of figurative language appears in the comparison?
exercises.explanation: Like marca una comparación explícita entre el sonido de la puerta y el de un corredor cansado.
exercises.hint: Fíjate en la función de like.

exercises.prompt:
Read the lines. “The courtyard has low brick walls and a round stone fountain. Long shadows stretch across the pale tiles.”

What type of writing is this?
exercises.explanation: El texto presenta detalles visuales del lugar, como formas, colores y sombras.
exercises.hint: Comprueba si el texto cuenta una secuencia de hechos o describe un lugar.

exercises.prompt:
Read the notice. “The city repaired the broken ramps last week. The new route lets visitors reach the playground without using stairs.”

What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To persuade readers to buy playground equipment.
To inform readers about a change in access.
To entertain readers with a story about the city.
To criticize visitors who use the playground.
exercises.explanation: La nota informa de la reparación y explica cómo facilita el acceso.
exercises.hint: Busca qué cambio se menciona y qué explica la segunda oración.

exercises.prompt:
“I read my name on the list and imagined the whole room laughing. During practice, I missed the first line twice. On Thursday, my brother sat in the front row with his notebook. I felt my face grow hot as I walked onstage. Then I spotted his smile and took a breath. The words came out, one by one.”

How does the tone change from the opening to the ending?
exercises.explanation: La narradora teme que el público se ría. Al final respira y logra hablar. El tono cambia de inquietud a alivio.
exercises.hint: Compara lo que imagina al inicio con lo que logra al final.

exercises.prompt:
Read the passage. “The bus stop needs a shelter. Riders wait in the rain, and the nearest covered area is two blocks away.”

What feature makes this passage argumentative?
options: It supports a proposal with reasons.
It describes a place without making a claim.
It lists events in the order they happened.
It gives a definition for a new term.
exercises.explanation: El texto propone instalar un refugio y apoya la propuesta con la lluvia y la distancia al lugar cubierto más cercano.
exercises.hint: Identifica una propuesta y las razones que la apoyan.

exercises.prompt:
Read the lines. “The empty station was silent. Rain ran down the glass roof, and water dripped onto the platform.”

Where does the scene take place?
exercises.explanation: El pasaje menciona una estación y su andén. Ambos detalles sitúan la escena en una estación.
exercises.hint: Busca las palabras que indican el lugar antes de identificar el ambiente.

exercises.prompt:
Read the passage. “I held the letter for a full minute before opening it. My hands shook. When I saw the word ACCEPTED, I ran downstairs to tell my sister.”

How does the narrator’s mood change?
exercises.explanation: La espera y el temblor muestran nervios al inicio. La noticia de la aceptación hace que la narradora corra a compartirla con su hermana.
exercises.hint: Compara las manos temblorosas con la reacción después de leer la carta.

title: Organización y transiciones
objective: Elige oraciones de inicio y cierre, ordena un párrafo y selecciona transiciones adecuadas.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 10 del PDF · Destrezas de redacción · Coherencia y claridad

exercises.prompt: Choose the best opening sentence. “____. Before each meeting, members collect recipes. During the meeting, they try one dish and share the result.”
options: The school kitchen has three windows.
After the meeting, the members put away the plates.
The cooking club learns by preparing a different dish at each meeting.
exercises.explanation: Presenta el club y su forma de aprender. Las frases siguientes describen cómo sus miembros eligen y preparan un plato.
exercises.hint: Busca la idea amplia que explica lo que hacen los miembros.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best transition. “The first bus was full. ____, we took the next one.”
exercises.explanation: Tomar el siguiente autobús fue consecuencia de que el primero estaba lleno. Therefore expresa ese resultado.
exercises.hint: Pregunta si la segunda oración presenta un motivo, un resultado o un ejemplo.

exercises.prompt:
Put the sentences in the best order.

(1) After the pot dried, she painted the outside. (2) Maya chose an old clay pot to use for herbs. (3) She cleared out the soil and rinsed the pot. (4) She let the damp pot dry in the sun.
exercises.explanation: Primero se presenta la maceta. Maya la vacía y enjuaga, la deja secar y al final la pinta.
exercises.hint: Relaciona el agua del enjuague con el secado que requiere la pintura.

exercises.prompt:
Which sentence does not belong in this paragraph?

(1) Our class organized a coat drive. (2) Volunteers collected coats in the gym. (3) The gym has a new scoreboard. (4) They delivered the coats to a shelter.
exercises.explanation: El marcador del gimnasio comparte el lugar, pero no explica cómo se reunieron o entregaron los abrigos.
exercises.hint: Determina si cada oración explica la campaña de abrigos.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best conclusion. “The town placed signs near two busy crossings. During the trial, more drivers slowed down at both places. ____.”
options: Every town in the world should ban cars.
Few people know how to read road signs.
At both crossings, more drivers slowed down after the signs went up.
Slower driving makes a road longer.
exercises.explanation: Resume el cambio observado y conserva los límites de la prueba en esos dos cruces.
exercises.hint: Busca una oración que cierre el texto dentro de los límites del ensayo.

exercises.prompt: Choose the transition that shows contrast. “The trail was steep. ____, the group finished the hike ahead of schedule.”
exercises.explanation: Nevertheless indica que el grupo terminó antes de lo previsto a pesar de la dificultad del camino.
exercises.hint: Busca la transición que equivale a «a pesar de eso».

exercises.prompt: Choose the best title. “Our class counted birds near the school garden for five mornings. Sparrows appeared every day. A hawk visited once. After each count, we added the numbers to a chart.”
options: A Week Caring for a Hawk
How to Grow a School Garden
Five Mornings of Bird Counts at School
exercises.explanation: El título presenta la actividad principal, el lugar y la duración. Las especies de aves son detalles de la observación.
exercises.hint: Busca un título que cubra todo el texto y conserve su duración.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best transition. “First, wash the apples. ____, cut them into thin slices.”
exercises.explanation: Next indica el paso que sigue. Aquí se cortan las manzanas después de lavarlas.
exercises.hint: La segunda instrucción sigue a la primera en el tiempo.

exercises.prompt:
A draft has four sentences. Which one should the writer remove to keep the paragraph focused on the new reading corner?

(1) The class set up a reading corner by the window. (2) Students brought cushions and a floor lamp. (3) They sorted donated books into baskets. (4) The school’s soccer team won a match on Friday.
exercises.explanation: Las primeras tres oraciones describen el lugar y su preparación. La cuarta cambia de tema a un partido de fútbol.
exercises.hint: Identifica la oración que no explica cómo prepararon el rincón de lectura.

title: Puntuación y edición de oraciones
objective: Reconoce la puntuación adecuada y edita frases para aplicar el vocabulario preciso y reducir repeticiones.
source: College Board, Guía de estudio PIENSE II (2019), p. 11 del PDF · Destrezas de redacción · Propiedad, corrección, precisión y concisión

exercises.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: After the rain, stopped we opened the windows.
After, the rain stopped we opened the windows.
After the rain stopped, we opened the windows.
After the rain stopped we, opened the windows.
exercises.explanation: La coma va después de toda la cláusula introductoria «After the rain stopped».
exercises.hint: Ubica dónde termina la introducción y empieza la acción principal.

exercises.prompt: Choose the most precise replacement for “looked at.” “The mechanic looked at each brake for signs of wear.”
exercises.explanation: Inspected indica que revisó los frenos con cuidado para detectar desgaste.
exercises.hint: Busca el verbo que expresa una revisión cuidadosa.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best way to combine these sentences. “The team recorded the temperatures. The team put the temperatures in a table.”
options: The temperatures recorded the team and put it in a table.
The team made a table instead of recording the temperatures.
The team put the table in the temperatures it recorded.
The team recorded the temperatures and put them in a table.
exercises.explanation: And une los dos verbos con el sujeto compartido. Them sustituye the temperatures y evita repetirlo.
exercises.hint: Conserva quién realizó ambas acciones y qué datos se registraron.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best punctuation. The location of the printer is extra information.
options: Our printer, which sits next to the window, needs a new cartridge.
Our printer which sits, next to the window needs a new cartridge.
Our printer, which sits next to the window needs a new cartridge.
Our printer which sits next to the window, needs, a new cartridge.
exercises.explanation: La cláusula explica dónde está la impresora y aporta un dato adicional. Dos comas señalan dónde empieza y termina.
exercises.hint: Quita el dato sobre la ventana y comprueba si la oración principal se entiende.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best edit to remove repetition. “We returned back to the classroom at noon.”
options: We entered the classroom at noon.
We returned to the classroom at noon.
We returned back to the classroom.
exercises.explanation: Returned ya indica que se volvió. La oración editada conserva el lugar y la hora.
exercises.hint: Mantén los datos de lugar y tiempo y elimina la palabra repetitiva.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best way to combine the sentences so the first idea explains the second. “The filter was clogged. The pump moved less water.”
options: The filter was clogged because the pump moved less water.
Because the filter was clogged, the pump moved less water.
The filter was clogged although the pump moved more water.
The pump clogged the filter before it moved less water.
exercises.explanation: Because convierte el filtro obstruido en la causa. El menor flujo de agua queda como el resultado.
exercises.hint: Comprueba qué condición produjo el cambio en el flujo.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated compound sentence.
options: The room was dark, so Lila switched on the lamp.
The room was dark, Lila switched on the lamp.
The room was dark so, Lila switched on the lamp.
The room, was dark so Lila switched on the lamp.
exercises.explanation: La coma va antes de so, que une dos oraciones completas y expresa un resultado.
exercises.hint: Localiza los dos sujetos y el conector que une las ideas.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct punctuation for a direct question.
options: Where did you leave the keys?
Where did you leave the keys.
Where, did you leave the keys?
Where did you leave the keys,
exercises.explanation: El signo de interrogación va al final. No se pone una coma entre where y did.
exercises.hint: Una pregunta directa termina con un signo de interrogación en inglés.

exercises.prompt: Choose the edit that keeps both actions and avoids unnecessary repetition. “Sana labeled the jars. Sana placed the jars on the shelf.”
options: Sana labeled the shelf and the jars.
Sana placed the jars on the shelf and never labeled them.
She placed the labels on the shelf with Sana.
Sana labeled the jars and placed them on the shelf.
exercises.explanation: Sana realiza las dos acciones. Them sustituye a the jars después de placed y conserva el sentido.
exercises.hint: Conserva un solo sujeto y usa un pronombre para la segunda mención de the jars.
